newsitem.title: USA: American Re CFO to resign March 1997.
newsitem.headline: American Re CFO to resign March 1997.

text.p: American Re Corp said chief financial officer James Fisher has decided to resign, effective March 31, 1997.
American Re said Fisher has agreed to remain as a consultant to American Re through January 1999.
American Re, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Munich Reinsurance Co, was bought out by the giant German reinsurer last year in a $3.3 billion deal.

"While we regret his resignation, we understand that, with the completion of our capital enhancement plans over the past four years, Jim would like to seek additional challenges outside of American Re," American Re chief executive Paul Inderbitzin said.
"We are fortunate to have him with us as CFO through the closing of our 1996 results and as a consultant into 1999," Inderbitzen said.
Although Fisher has played an important role at American Re, Wall Street analysts said they did not think Fisher's departure would be a significant blow to Munich Re.
"I think what Munich Re was buying was a team that had good client relationships and that would certainly be the frontline people," Salomon Brothers analyst Michael Smith said.
Lehman analyst Peter Wade agreed. "I don't think it will have a significant impact on Munich Re," he said.
In a statement, Fisher said "the last ten-and-a-half years have been extraordinarily rewarding from both a personal and professional standpoint.

"I am gratified that the American Re I helped to build has become a member of one of the world's premier financial service companies, and I am thrilled that we will continue to have an on-going relationship."

Earlier this year, Mary Hennessy resigned her post as chief actuary at American Re and was appointed to the newly-created position of executive vice president and chief underwriting officer at TIG Holdings Inc.
